land.text: Britain, Gaul and Spain as the Roman Empire held them in 382: 'ruled Britain, Gaul, and Spain'

predecessors.note: Gratian's western empire: Maximus was 'proclaimed emperor in Britannia' in 383 and Gratian 'was killed at Lyon on 25 August 383'. The roman-empire dossier carries the matching losses (counterpart 'Magnus Maximus (usurper)').

Italy, which Maximus invaded in 387 and from which Valentinian II 'fled with his mother and court to Theodosius I'

land.text: Britain, Gaul, Spain and, from 387, Italy: after the Battle of Poetovio in 388 Valentinian II 'ruled from Gaul after being restored to power in 388' and Theodosius I held the East

successors.note: The pages say Theodosius 'recovered Italy' (roman-empire dossier) and Valentinian II was installed at Vienne in Gaul; neither opened page says what happened in Britain and Spain in 388.

capitals.name: Augusta Treverorum (Trier)
capitals.note: 'Maximus made his capital at Augusta Treverorum'; the page gives no year, so the start is bridged from the 383 move to Gaul. He was proclaimed in Britain (Segontium in north Wales is the Roman Britain page's place, not opened here).

rulers.name: Magnus Maximus
rulers.title: usurper emperor
rulers.note: Proclaimed in Britannia in 383 (spring, per the body text); recognised as Augustus of the West by an accord that 'seems to have been reached in 384'; surrendered at Aquileia and died 28 August 388. His son Victor was executed by Arbogast at Trier in autumn 388.

correction.text: Britain, Gaul and Spain as the Roman Empire held them in 382: 'ruled Britain, Gaul, and Spain'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no row for Maximus; its Roman Empire shapes 383-386 and 387-389 keep the whole West. The Magnus Maximus page: 'ruled Britain, Gaul, and Spain' while 'Maximus acknowledged Valentinian's rule of Italy, Africa and Illyricum' (the 384 accord); the Valentinian II page: Maximus 'established his headquarters in Gaul and Hispania'. The page notes a conflict: its lead lists Hispania among Valentinian's holdings. The region is the Britain, Gaul and Hispania regions cut to the Roman Empire's 382 shape. Neither page gives an area.

union.text: Britain, Gaul and Spain as the Roman Empire held them in 382: 'ruled Britain, Gaul, and Spain'
Italy, which Maximus invaded in 387 and from which Valentinian II 'fled with his mother and court to Theodosius I'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'In 387, Maximus's ambitions led him to invade Italy' (Magnus Maximus page); the Valentinian II page: 'In 386 to 387, Maximus crossed the Alps into the Po valley to threaten Milan' and Valentinian II 'fled' to Theodosius at Thessalonica. Neither page says in so many words that Maximus held Italy, only that the emperor of Italy fled; the page gives no month. Africa and Illyricum stay with Valentinian II (sic, per the 384 accord) and are not drawn.

region.text: Britannia, where he 'was proclaimed emperor' in 383

ledger.note: 383: Magnus Maximus is proclaimed emperor in Britain. 'In 383, he was proclaimed emperor in Britannia' (spring of 383 in the body text); the Valentinian II page: 'commander of the armies in Britain, declared himself Emperor'.
383: the seat moves to Trier. 'Maximus made his capital at Augusta Treverorum'; the page gives no year, so the move is bridged from his crossing to Gaul in 383.

region.text: Hispania: 'established his headquarters in Gaul and Hispania' (Valentinian II page); 'ruled Britain, Gaul, and Spain' (Magnus Maximus page)

ledger.note: 383: Hispania follows Gaul. 'In 383, Magnus Maximus ... declared himself Emperor' and 'established his headquarters in Gaul and Hispania'. The Magnus Maximus page notes the conflict that its lead lists Hispania among Valentinian's holdings; the year of the acquisition is the page's 383 context, not a dated sentence.

region.text: Gaul, to which 'Maximus went to ... to pursue his imperial ambitions' and where Gratian 'was killed at Lyon on 25 August 383'

ledger.note: 25 August 383: Gratian is killed at Lyon and Gaul passes to Maximus. 'was killed at Lyon on 25 August 383'; the page gives no date for the crossing and does not say in a sentence that Gaul passed to him, so the region is the researcher's reading of 'ruled Britain, Gaul, and Spain'.

region.text: Italy, which Maximus invaded in 387 and from which Valentinian II 'fled with his mother and court to Theodosius I'

ledger.note: 387: Maximus invades Italy and Valentinian II flees. 'In 387, Maximus's ambitions led him to invade Italy'; the young emperor 'fled with his mother and court to Theodosius I'. The pages do not say that he took or held Italy, nor give a month; the Valentinian II page has the crossing of the Alps into the Po valley 'to threaten Milan' in '386 to 387'.

region.text: the campaign of Theodosius I 'June-August 388', ending at the Battle of Poetovio (Ptuj)

ledger.note: June 388: Theodosius I marches west against Maximus. The page says the campaign ran June-August 388 and names 'his defeat by Theodosius I at the Battle of Poetovio in 388'; Valentinian II page: 'Theodosius and his forces marched west in 388 and defeated Maximus'. Poetovio (modern Ptuj) is placed in Slovenia from the modern name, not from the page.
August 388: Maximus surrenders at Aquileia and is executed. 'Maximus surrendered in Aquileia' and was executed; the page gives his death as 28 August 388 and no execution date.

union.text: Britain, Gaul and Spain as the Roman Empire held them in 382: 'ruled Britain, Gaul, and Spain'
Italy, which Maximus invaded in 387 and from which Valentinian II 'fled with his mother and court to Theodosius I'

ledger.note: 28 August 388: Maximus is dead and his domain ends. 'Valentinian II ruled from Gaul after being restored to power in 388' (Valentinian II page: installed 'at Vienne in Gaul'); the pages do not say who took Britain and Spain in 388, nor that Theodosius took direct control of Maximus's former territory.

wars.name: Campaign of Theodosius I against Magnus Maximus (Battle of Poetovio)

zones.text: Poetovio, where Maximus was defeated in 388

wars.outcome: Theodosius I defeated Maximus at the Battle of Poetovio in 388; Maximus surrendered at Aquileia and was executed on 28 August 388, and Valentinian II was restored in Gaul.
wars.note: The Valentinian II page gives 'In 386 to 387' for the crossing of the Alps; the Magnus Maximus page '387'. No page opened mentions a Battle of the Save.

certainty.note: The realm is named by provinces, never by boundaries: whether Hispania was held and how much of Italy are the pages' vague statements.

sources.title: Magnus Maximus
sources.note: Proclamation 383, Gratian at Lyon 25 Aug 383, Trier, the 384 accord, 387 invasion, Poetovio 388, death 28 Aug 388.

sources.title: Valentinian II
sources.note: Maximus's headquarters in Gaul and Hispania, 386-387 crossing of the Alps, Valentinian restored at Vienne in 388.

notes: A rebel state Cliopatria lacks, written because the roman-empire dossier's 383-388 events name 'Magnus Maximus (usurper)' as counterpart. Two pages opened; the extent of the realm is vague on both: 'ruled Britain, Gaul, and Spain' (Magnus Maximus page) against its own lead listing Hispania with Valentinian's lands; the Valentinian II page has Valentinian ruling 'Italy (part of Illyricum) and North Africa'. Neither page gives an area or the date of Maximus's crossing to Gaul or of Valentinian's flight. The region is the Britain, Gaul and Hispania regions intersected with Cliopatria's Roman Empire shape of 382 so the Rhine frontier follows the empire's. Wikidata id unknown. Gazetteer: 'Poetovio' (Ptuj) and 'Segontium' are not place names; Slovenia stands in for Poetovio. The roman-empire dossier's own 388 entries ('Britain and Gaul come back') are bridged by the same silence.
